meta.title_plain: How Alexander Zverev turned a tennis family into Olympic gold
meta.teaser: Zverev grew up with two tennis-pro parents, won Olympic gold and kept chasing Grand Slams.

page.title: How Alexander Zverev turned a tennis family into Olympic gold
page.bigIdea: Zverev lost his first three Grand Slam finals. He kept going and finally won two in 2026, proving that losing a final is a step, not the end.

cards.title: A whole family of pros
cards.front: Alexander was born in Hamburg, Germany, in 1997. Tennis was the family business.
cards.back: Both his parents were pro players for the Soviet Union. His mum, Irina, was a top Soviet player. His big brother Mischa became a pro too.
cards.tryit: Ask someone at home to feed you 20 balls. Count how many you return deep.

cards.title: Best junior in the world
cards.front: He started playing at about age three. By 16 he was the top junior.
cards.back: He was the world's No. 1 junior at the end of 2013. In 2014 he won the Australian Open boys' title.
cards.tryit: Write down one junior goal for this season, like a ranking or a tournament.

cards.title: First title at 19
cards.front: In 2016 he won his first pro tournament, in St. Petersburg.
cards.back: He beat Stan Wawrinka, a Grand Slam champion, in the final. In 2018 he beat Novak Djokovic to win the ATP Finals.
cards.tryit: Play a practice set against someone better than you. Note one shot that worked.

cards.title: Gold at the Olympics
cards.front: At the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, he came from behind against world No. 1 Djokovic.
cards.back: Then he beat Karen Khachanov 6-3, 6-1 in the final. He joined Steffi Graf as the only Germans with Olympic singles gold.
cards.tryit: Practise one comeback: start a game at 0-30 and try to win it.

cards.title: Three losses, then two wins
cards.front: Zverev lost Grand Slam finals in 2020, 2024 and 2025. Many people doubted him.
cards.back: In 2026 he finally won the French Open and the US Open. He beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final.
cards.tryit: Think of a match you lost. Write one thing you'd change next time.

words.d: The best-ranked player in the world under age 18.

Winning all four Grand Slams and Olympic gold in one year.
Winning after being behind in the score.

quiz.q: What was special about Zverev's parents?
opts: They were both pro tennis players
quiz.hint: Look at card 1. Tennis was the family business.
quiz.why: Both his parents played pro tennis for the Soviet Union, and his brother turned pro too.

quiz.q: Which junior title did Zverev win in 2014?
quiz.hint: It's the first Grand Slam of every year.
quiz.why: He won the 2014 Australian Open boys' singles after finishing 2013 as junior No. 1.

quiz.q: Who did Zverev beat in the Tokyo Olympics semifinal?
quiz.hint: He was world No. 1 and chasing a Golden Slam.
quiz.why: Zverev came back to beat Djokovic, then beat Khachanov in the final.

quiz.q: What does Zverev's story teach about losing finals?
quiz.hint: Count his lost finals, then look at 2026.
quiz.why: He lost three Grand Slam finals but kept improving and won two in 2026.

page.think: Zverev lost big finals before he won one. What's a loss you've had that could help you win next time?
